contexts.text: Women who have died old and worn out with old age ... (there) come more and more into the bloom of youth... and into a beauty which surpasses all conception...
Thou shalt be buried in a good old age () = the fruition of all goods by those who are the Lord's. AC 1854, Explained.
Abraham and Sarah were old () = the human with the Lord, that it should be put off. Explained.
Old age involves nothing but the last time... (and) nothing whatever of old age... For what old age is they do not know in the other life.
To grow old () = to put off the human; thus to change the state. AC 2204. AC 2209.
From a boy and even to an old man () = falsities and evils recent and confirmed... Old men = those who have attained to great age, thus things confirmed. Illustrated.
Old men () confirmed truths; old women = confirmed goods.
Our father is old () = that it is no longer known what good is.
To his old age () = when the days were fulfilled that the human should be put off; (for) old age = the state when the human should be put off and the Divine put on. AC 2625:3. AC 2644.
The states of the Church are like the ages of man... the fourth of which is old age; (and which) is called the fulness, or end. AC 2905:3. Described.

Abraham was old... () = when the state was at hand that the Human of the Lord should be made Divine... (For) old, or old age = to put off what is human, and to put on what is heavenly; and, when predicated of the Lord, to put on the Divine... The reason is that with the Angels there is no idea of old age... but an idea of the state as to life in which they are; and therefore when... old age is mentioned in the Word, the Angels who are with the man can have no other idea than one of the state of life in which they are, and in which men are when they are passing through their ages even to the last; namely, that they are successively putting off what is human, and putting on what is heavenly.

This last state (into which men come as they advance in years) which is signified by old men, is a state of wisdom, in which is the innocence of infancy. Thus the first state and the last are united; and man, when old, as again an infant, but wise, is introduced into the Lord's Kingdom.

In a good old age, old, and full () = a new state of representation. Old age = to put off the old, and to put on the new... because with the Angels... there is no idea of time... but instead they have an idea of states; as... instead of old age an idea of a state of wisdom; and as then man passes from the things of time to those of a life without time, and thus puts on a new state, by old age is signified what is new; and, here, a new representative...

Isaac became old () = when the state was at hand. To become old = the presence of a new state; for old age, in the Word, = both the putting off of a former state, and the putting on of a new state; and this for the reason that old age is the last of age, when the corporeal things begin to be put off, and, with them, the loves of the preceding age; and thus when the interiors begin to be illustrated... and also because the Angels... have no longer an idea of any old age; but, instead of it, the idea of a new life; thus, here, the idea that the state (here treated of) was at hand.
Old and full of days () = what is new of life.

Because he was the son of his old ages () = his own life in him: (for) old age = the putting off of a former state and the glutting on of a new state; also, what is new of life. For old age, in the internal sense does not = old age, because the internal man, or spirit of man, does not know what old age is; but, as the body or external man becomes old, he passes into what is new of life... (Thus) by old age, in the internal sense, is signified life.
Old men () = the wise.
To old age, and to grey hairs () = to the last of the Church.
Old men () = the wise.
When man becomes old... the innocence of wisdom conjoins itself with the innocence of ignorance which he had had in infancy; and thus, as a true infant, he passes into the other life.
A child of his old ages, the youngest () = derivative truth which is new... Old age = what is new of life.
Through old age () = because in the end of the representation; (for) old age = what is new of representation; thus the end of the former one.
Old men () = the wise. References.
Peter when old = the faith of the Church as it is in its end. AE 195:14. AE 820:7.
Old men, in the Word, = those who are in wisdom; thus who are in the life of good from the doctrine of truth.
The head = evil; in like manner the old and honoured ().
That then evil and falsity will lead, is signified by when thou shalt be old... ().

Man is so created that... when he becomes old he may be in internal innocence... and therefore when man becomes old he decreases in body, and becomes again like an infant, but wise; thus an Angel... Hence in the Word... an old man = a wise man in whom is innocence.
Other Spirits (are with man) in his old age... In old age, there are present Spirits who are in wisdom and in innocence; thus who communicate with the Inmost... Heaven.
(Those who die as old men enter the Spiritual World as old men, but the state is afterwards changed.)
The delight of love truly conjugial not only lasts to old age in the world...
In a word, to grow old in Heaven is to grow young. DP 324:4.
(Images of old men, with the Ancients, = wisdom.)
These (virgins and youths) in the world had been decrepit old people.
A friendship emulative of conjugial friendship when they become old. CL 290:end, Described.
An old man who was afterwards seen as a young one, for he was an Angel from Heaven.
When man verges to old age...
Old men () = wisdom which is of good; elders, truths which are from good; young men, intelligence. AE 412:23.
The old man () = wisdom which is of good.
To remove the diviner and the old man () = to remove all intelligence and wisdom.
Old men () = wisdom.
Old man and infant = wisdom and innocence.
Old man = the intelligence of truth; the honoured = the wisdom of good.
Old men = those who are in wisdom.
Old males and old women () = the intelligent and the wise. ( = those intelligent from doctrine and from the affection of truth. AE 727:9.)
An old man and full of days = wisdom.
Old age = wisdom.
Old man = wisdom. AE 863:9.
Old man = wisdom.
Old man = falsities confirmed.
Wives worn out with old age become young women.
